Subject: Dedicated capacity options and ramp (proposal attached)

Hi Elena / Samir —

Thanks again for the call this morning. As discussed, attached is a concise set of dedicated reservation options tied to the volumes you shared (avg tokens / peak QPS) and the three-stage ramp you outlined. The attachment (redwood_dedicated_proposal_nebulagen_v1.pdf) includes cluster sizing, minimum-gpu anchor, pricing deltas, and a recommended warmup credit program. I also attached gpu-slate-nebulagen.xlsx with the exact GPU SKU mapping for the three proposal options.

Quick summary (high-level):
- Option 1 — Light Anchor: 8 x A100-equivalent min (soft floor), 4-week ramp to target. Lower unit price; limited reserved throughput. Good if early traffic uncertainty.
- Option 2 — Balanced Anchor: 16 x A100-equivalent min (soft floor + utilization credits), 6–8 week staged ramp. Better latency SLO headroom, recommended for sustained production.
- Option 3 — Anchored Slate: 24 x A100-equivalent min (hard floor) with phased 12-week ramp and guaranteed burst lanes. Best for predictable latency at scale; includes warm start credits for first 6 weeks.

Key trade-offs I want to surface:
- Soft floor vs hard floor: soft floors give you flexibility (lower initial commit) but come with a utilization-credit mechanism so you can bank unused committed cycles as credit toward future invoices. Hard floors simplify capacity planning but increase committed burn.
- Warmup/prewarm credits: we propose 25% free warmup credits on Option 3 (applied to first 6 weeks) to offset engineering e2e testing and flash warmup cost.
- SLA/availability: all options include our standard Dedicated SLA; Option 3 includes an elevated latency target and higher uptime SLA (SLA addendum in the PDF).

As next steps: can you confirm a preferred anchor option (1/2/3), and whether procurement prefers soft-floor constructs (with utilization reconciliation) or hard-floor fixed commitments? Once we have that, we'll put together a redlined commercial term sheet for legal and a targeted onboarding calendar.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call to walk the sheet line-by-line.

Best,

Ava / Ben —

Looping in a couple suggested commercial guardrails that tend to close quickly with customers like Nebulagen:

1) Utilization-credit mechanics (recommended): monthly reconciliation where unused committed dollars convert to a credit bucket at face value and can be applied to future invoices for up to 12 months. Credits are applied before any overage charge. This keeps procurement happy (dollar-denominated credit) while preserving soft-floor flexibility.

2) Soft-floor plus runway: Offer Option 2 as a "soft anchor" at 16 min GPUs with an 8-week ramp milestone schedule. If Nebulagen hits the midpoint utilization (70% of target) continuously for 3 weeks by week-6, we automatically greenlight the next tranche without a contract amendment. If not, credits are reconciled and they retain the soft floor.

3) Onboarding/on-ramp credit: Offer a one-time 10% onboarding credit (dollar discount) on the first three months' committed dollars if they sign to Option 2 within the next 14 days. This is a short-lived incentive to align deadlines for board approval.

4) Ops runbook extract: Ben — can you pull the "Dedicated Ops Escalation" 1-page and attach? Elena: we can include that as an addendum to the contract.

Pricing impact (high-level): the onboarding credit reduces ARR by ~2.5% in year-1; the utilization-credit is budget-neutral (credits roll-forward) but affects monthly cashflow.

If Ava/Ben are okay, I recommend offering Option 2 with the above guardrails and the onboarding credit to keep momentum.

- Ops Escalation Addendum: See attached "Dedicated Ops Escalation (1-pg).pdf" (we'll include in the DocuSign packet).

Attachments included in this update: margin-analysis.xlsx (internal breakouts) and a 1-page ops extract will be appended to the DocuSign. I'll create the DocuSign packet and post the link here once legal has applied the standard SOW boilerplate.
